info.name: Mini ERP + CRM Operations Portal
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Mini ERP + CRM API (Phase 8).

**Setup**
1. Import this collection and `Mini-ERP-CRM.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the *Mini ERP + CRM — Local* environment.
3. Run **Auth → Login (admin)**. It stores `{{token}}`; collection-level auth applies it to every other request, so nothing is pasted by hand.

**Where to start** — the *Workflow (end-to-end)* folder runs the whole story top to bottom: create a customer, create a product with opening stock, raise a challan, confirm it, and watch stock fall by exactly the quantity sold with a ledger row explaining why.

**Errors (these fail on purpose)** demonstrates the 4xx contract. Its tests assert the failures, so a green run there means the error handling is right.

Full reference: `docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md`.

item.description: The ledger is append-only: no update, no delete. A mistake is corrected by recording the opposite movement, which leaves both entries visible.

item.description: A DRAFT never touches stock. Confirming deducts every line atomically and writes one OUT movement per line. Line items carry a snapshot of the product, so a later rename or reprice cannot rewrite a dispatched document.

item.name: Errors (these fail on purpose)
item.description: The documented 4xx contract, demonstrable rather than merely described. Every request here is expected to fail — the tests assert the failure.

request.description: Unknown email, wrong password and a deactivated account all return exactly this, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which accounts exist.
Uses {{warehouseToken}} — run "Auth → Login (warehouse)" first.
/customers/abc is not a resource address at all, so it is a 400 — not the 422 a bad body or query would get.
Body, params and query are validated in one pass, so nothing is fixed one round trip at a time.

item.name: 422 — limit above 100 is rejected, not clamped

request.description: A client that asks for 500 rows should learn that it will not get them.
Unknown fields are normally stripped, which would make this look like it worked. The field is declared purely so it can be rejected with the rule attached.

item.name: 422 — the same product twice on one challan

request.description: Silently summing the lines would hide a data-entry mistake the user should see.
Assumes the seeded catalogue. SKUs are compared upper-cased.

item.name: 409 — insufficient stock on a manual OUT

request.description: The transaction rolls back: no stock moves and no ledger row is written. The message names the product and both numbers.
The goods have already left. Silently adding stock back would let anyone inflate inventory by confirming and cancelling in a loop — a stock return is a separate flow.
